title: Choose the visual world for the dashboard (safer hand)
question: The familiar end of the spectrum: three conventional directions and the category standard. You pick.

options.label: Research Report (DORA style)
options.lineage: Google's State of DevOps / DORA reports, the engineering-leadership reference
options.thesis: The snapshot as a short research report: a headline finding, a few annotated charts, and a methods section, the format engineering leaders already trust.
options.viewport: A report cover band with the finding as its title, three key-finding numbers beneath, then the first annotated chart (where the 7.3 days go), with byline and snapshot date.
options.risk: Familiar and credible, and close to what many research pages look like; it earns trust more than it surprises.

options.label: Data-Journalism Briefing
options.thesis: A short, chart-led explainer: each finding a headline sentence over one annotated chart, labels written directly on the data.
options.viewport: A headline ('Kubernetes pull requests wait for review, not for merging'), a one-line standfirst, then a full-width annotated bar of where the time goes.
options.risk: Reads as journalism, so the drill-down tool feel is secondary; the FT salmon tint would be borrowed clothing and must be our own.

options.label: Engineering Status Page
options.lineage: service status pages (GitHub Status, Atlassian Statuspage)
options.thesis: Each review stage listed like a service on a status page, with its current queue, wait and a row of history ticks, so the stuck stage reads like a degraded service.
options.viewport: A banner ('Review: 368 PRs waiting, median 69 days'), then one row per stage with its status, queue size and wait, the brief below as an incident note.
options.risk: Instantly readable to engineers, but status language (degraded, outage) can sound like blame and implies live monitoring this snapshot doesn't do.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: An engineering-metrics dashboard executed to the craft of Swarmia, LinearB and Linear's insights views.
canonCard.viewport: Headline tiles, then the brief, the ranked table and the charts, refined to that level of finish.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every analytics product by design.
